change_sets.summary: Proposed 3 claims, 1 concept, 2 predictions, 1 question and 1 evidence item from Pachocki's "An Alien Mind" (openai.com returned 403, so content is grounded via secondary coverage: StartupHub.ai, the Ask Who Casts AI podcast page, and search snippets), plus 4 relations.

proposed_operations.payload: {"op":"create_thought","thought":{"type":"claim","status":"tentative","title":"Modern AI is grown, not designed","statement":"Jakub Pachocki (OpenAI Chief Scientist, \"An Alien Mind\", 2026-09-06) argues that current AI systems are grown more than designed: they emerge from running a simple optimization step over enormous compute, and progress is driven primarily by compute scaling rather than algorithmic breakthroughs. The consequence is an intelligence whose internals its builders do not fully understand."}}
proposed_operations.rationale: The essay's foundational framing; everything else (opacity, monitoring difficulty) follows from it.

proposed_operations.payload: {"op":"create_thought","thought":{"type":"claim","status":"tentative","title":"CoT monitoring becomes unreliable as reasoning merges with tool use","statement":"Pachocki claims that chain-of-thought monitoring, a key current oversight technique for reasoning models, becomes unreliable as model reasoning merges with tool use and as the reasoning process generalizes beyond legible text. If true, labs may soon lose their main window into what models are actually doing."}}
proposed_operations.rationale: A specific, challengeable technical claim about why current oversight methods degrade.

proposed_operations.payload: {"op":"create_thought","thought":{"type":"concept","status":"tentative","title":"Goal alignment vs value alignment","statement":"Pachocki separates alignment into goal alignment (the model reliably follows the instructions it is given) and value alignment (the model independently maintains principles such as honesty even when not instructed to). Per secondary coverage of the essay, he holds that current safety measures are brittle on both dimensions."}}
proposed_operations.rationale: Load-bearing distinction the essay uses to structure its alignment discussion.

proposed_operations.payload: {"op":"create_thought","thought":{"type":"prediction","status":"tentative","title":"Current pace of progress will sustain into recursive self-improvement","statement":"Pachocki writes that internal OpenAI results give him a strong expectation that the current speed of progress can be sustained into recursive self-improvement, where AI increasingly drives its own development. Operationalized here as: by end of 2028, a frontier lab publicly attributes a majority of its research/engineering progress on its next model to AI systems. Probability is Pachocki's implied confidence, not an independent estimate.","confidence":{"probability":0.6,"resolveBy":"2028-12-31"}}}
proposed_operations.rationale: The essay's central forward-looking expectation; framed as a prediction so it can be scored.

proposed_operations.payload: {"op":"create_thought","thought":{"type":"claim","status":"tentative","title":"No lab has solved alignment well enough to keep scaling at max speed","statement":"Pachocki states that no lab has solved alignment and monitoring to a sufficient degree to continue responsibly scaling at maximum speed for much longer, and that \"the idea of racing forward at all costs seems absurd once one internalizes the seriousness of the stakes.\" This is notable as a statement from the chief scientist of a lab that has been racing."}}
proposed_operations.rationale: The essay's normative core — the statement that led to coverage of it as a case for slowing down.

proposed_operations.payload: {"op":"create_thought","thought":{"type":"prediction","status":"tentative","title":"Voluntary scaling slowdowns will become commonplace","statement":"Pachocki expects voluntary slowdowns by frontier labs to become commonplace until shared safety bars are established. Operationalized: by end of 2027, at least two frontier labs publicly announce delaying or pausing a training run or release explicitly on alignment/monitoring grounds.","confidence":{"probability":0.4,"resolveBy":"2027-12-31"}}}
proposed_operations.rationale: A falsifiable expectation about industry behavior distinct from the safety claim itself.

proposed_operations.payload: {"op":"create_thought","thought":{"type":"question","status":"tentative","title":"What concretely triggers a unilateral scaling pause?","statement":"The essay does not specify what benchmark would make monitoring reliable enough to justify continued scaling, nor what observable condition would trigger a unilateral pause; without such criteria, can 'voluntary slowdowns' be distinguished from ordinary release scheduling?"}}
proposed_operations.rationale: Gap flagged in secondary coverage (StartupHub.ai): the essay calls for pausing but gives no trigger criteria.

proposed_operations.payload: {"op":"create_thought","thought":{"type":"evidence","status":"tentative","title":"OpenAI concealed o1-preview reasoning chains","statement":"Per StartupHub.ai's coverage of the essay, Pachocki notes that OpenAI deliberately hid o1-preview's raw reasoning chains from users, and traces reasoning-model work to a mid-2023 internal project (RLSlow). The concealment is consistent with treating unfiltered chain-of-thought as a monitoring channel to be protected from optimization pressure.","source":"https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/ai-research/2026/jakub-pachocki-an-alien-mind-warns-of-rsi-risk"}}
proposed_operations.rationale: Concrete historical fact cited in coverage of the essay; bears on how seriously OpenAI has treated CoT legibility.
Monitoring difficulty follows from systems being grown rather than designed.
Failing CoT monitoring is a main reason given for why max-speed scaling is not yet responsible.
The slowdown prediction rests on labs accepting that alignment is unsolved.
OpenAI's own handling of o1 CoT shows it treats CoT as a monitoring channel worth protecting, which supports the claim that its degradation matters.
